### PRODUCT & ARCHITECTURE

**Q: What's your tech stack?**
> Next.js frontend, Python/FastAPI backend, Gemini AI for contract parsing and disclosure analysis, SQLite for persistence, NADAC API for real-time drug pricing benchmarks. All cloud-deployable, no on-prem requirements for the employer.

**Q: How does the disclosure ingestion actually work?**
> Employer or broker uploads the PBM's fee disclosure document — PDF, Word, whatever format it comes in. Our AI parses it, extracts the compensation structure (direct fees, indirect compensation, spread pricing arrangements, rebate terms), and scores each required element against what the DOL rule mandates. Missing or vague sections get flagged automatically with specific language about what's deficient.

**Q: How do you benchmark claims data?**
> We cross-reference every claim against the CMS NADAC database — that's the National Average Drug Acquisition Cost, updated weekly. We calculate the spread between what the plan paid and what the pharmacy's actual acquisition cost was, broken out by channel: retail, mail order, specialty, PBM-owned pharmacy. That's how we surface spread pricing.

**Q: What format does the output come in?**
> Right now it's an interactive dashboard with exportable reports. Each module generates findings with severity ratings — critical, warning, informational. We also auto-generate audit request letters when anomalies exceed thresholds. Working toward PDF board-ready reports as a next feature based on exactly what employers need to present to their benefits committee.

**Q: Can it handle different PBM disclosure formats? Every PBM reports differently.**
> That's exactly the problem we're solving. There's no standardized format yet — the DOL rule requires specific categories of information but doesn't prescribe a template. Our AI parser is trained to extract the required data points regardless of how the PBM structures the document. If a PBM buries compensation details in footnotes or uses vague umbrella terms, we flag that as a completeness gap.

**Q: What about data security? Employers are handling PHI.**
> Claims data contains PHI, so we're building with HIPAA compliance as a baseline requirement. Data encrypted at rest and in transit, no claims data stored permanently unless the employer opts in, and we're working toward SOC 2 and HITRUST certification pre-launch. The employer controls their data — we process it, we don't own it.
